newsitem.title: USA: CBOT traders say USDA data bullish for soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT traders say USDA data bullish for soybeans.

text.p: CBOT traders said the monthly supply/demand report released Friday by USDA was bullish for soybeans and supportive for corn and wheat.
Soybeans were expected to open up six to 12 cents a bushel and corn up three to five cents.
Wheat was called four to 10 cents higher, with additional support stemming from growing concern about forecasts for crop damaging cold weather in hard red winter wheat growing areas over the weekend.

USDA cut its forecast for 1996/97 soybean ending stocks to 125 million bushels from a previous projection of 140 million. Corn ending stocks were cut to 909 million bushels from a previous forecast of 959 million.
"They took 50 off corn and 15 off beans, the tightening of stocks continues and the weather problems will boost it with talk of a hard frost over the weekend," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Wheat ending stocks were also cut slightly to 460 million bushels from a previous 474 million.
Several private analytical firms have said drought damaged crops in both countries and production could fall.
"Those numbers could be lowered more," Luth said. "The Brazilian crop might by under 26 (million tonnes) and Argentina under 12 (million)."
Analysts said the soybean market could soon test its recent eight year high of $8.88-1/2 on the May contract.
"What it means is we have to go up and those highs we had in are going to go by the wayside. We're going to be sharply higher," Roose of U.S. Commodities said, speaking of the longer term effects.
May closed Thursday at $8.55-1/4 a bushel. It has a 30-cent daily trading limit.
